chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Isma'il ibn Mihran from Saif ibn 'Amirah from 'Amr ibn Shimir from Jabir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever seeks the pleasure of people by that which angers Allah, his praiser among the people will be a blamer. And whoever prefers the obedience of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by that which angers people, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will suffice him against the enmity of every enemy, the envy of every envier, and the aggression of every aggressor, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will be for him a supporter and a helper.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to a person who seeks people's pleasure by disobeying God?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on *Amr bi-l-Ma'ruf*, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) highlights the theological principle that divine satisfaction supersedes social conformity. It serves as a practical guide for maintaining religious integrity (*istiqama*) in communal settings, assuring believers that prioritizing God’s will shields them from the envy and hostility of others.
